'''Mystery Schools and Religious Movements: a Catalogue from Antiquity to Today''' lists, as fully as we can, the initiatory schools, mystery cults, esoteric orders and unusual religious movements of history and of the present — each with its dates, founder or centre, core teaching and status today. It is a catalogue, described neutrally in each movement's own terms; describing a group is not endorsing it, and groups that ended in harm are named as such. For the themes behind them, see [[Mystery Schools]]. Alpha — additions welcome.

|-

|-
| Hermeticism || Egypt (Greek texts, 1st–3rd c. CE) || ''Corpus Hermeticum''; knowledge (gnosis) of the divine mind || revived from 1463 (Ficino) to today
|-

|-

== 6. Movements that ended in harm ==
Named so the record is complete:
* '''Peoples Temple''' (Jim Jones) — over 900 dead at Jonestown, 1978.
* '''Branch Davidians''' — Waco siege, 1993.
* '''Order of the Solar Temple''' — murders and suicides, 1994–1997.
* '''Aum Shinrikyo''' — sarin attack on the Tokyo subway, 1995.
* '''Heaven's Gate''' — 39 suicides, 1997.

== 7. Esotericists who influenced politics ==
Influence, not endorsement — several of these fed movements that did great harm, and that is stated.
* '''John Dee''' (1527–1608) — mathematician, astrologer and angel-magician; adviser to Elizabeth I on navigation and empire (he popularised the phrase "British Empire").
* '''Freemasonry and the American founders''' — Washington, Franklin and many signers were Masons; Masonic ideals of fraternity and reason ran through the Enlightenment, though claims of a Masonic plot are legend.
* '''Grigori Rasputin''' (1869–1916) — mystic healer at the Russian court; his influence over the Tsarina damaged the monarchy before 1917.
* '''Annie Besant''' (1847–1933) — President of the Theosophical Society; founded the All-India Home Rule League (1916) and presided over the Indian National Congress (1917).
* '''Ariosophy''' — Guido von List and Jörg Lanz von Liebenfels (''Ostara'') mixed occultism with racial mythology in Austria and Germany; the '''Thule Society''' (1918) was among the circles around the early Nazi party. The SS '''Ahnenerbe''' (1935) later sponsored pseudo-archaeology. The "Vril society" is a later fiction.
* '''René Guénon''' (1886–1951) — founder of the Traditionalist school: a primordial Tradition behind all religions and a modern world in decline.
* '''Julius Evola''' (1898–1974) — Italian esotericist; led the UR Group (''Ur'', ''Krur'', 1927–29) on magic and initiation; his ''Revolt Against the Modern World'' (1934) and writings on race and the state were read in Fascist circles, though Mussolini kept him at a distance; after the war he influenced the Italian and European far right.
* '''Nicholas Roerich''' (1874–1947) — painter and Theosophist; the Roerich Pact (1935) to protect cultural monuments; his circle's letters with Henry Wallace (U.S. Secretary of Agriculture, later Vice President) — the "guru letters" — became a scandal in 1948.
* '''Aleister Crowley''' (1875–1947) — founder of Thelema; claims that he worked for British intelligence are debated.

== 8. Patterns ==
* Initiation in '''grades''' (Mithras' seven, Masonic degrees, Golden Dawn grades) mirrors a journey of the soul.
* Teachings attributed to '''hidden masters''' (Mahatmas, Ascended Masters, the Secret Chiefs) recur from Theosophy to the "I AM" line.
* '''Sacraments''' — kykeon at Eleusis, peyote, ayahuasca, ganja — sit at the centre of several, and some now have legal protection (see [[Religious Sacraments RFRA and the Temple of True Inner Light]]).
* Many claim descent from '''ancient Egypt''' or a lost temple lineage — see [[The Temple Lineage Hypothesis (Van Kush Ancestry)]].
